title: Dolly Left
description: A dolly left, also called a truck left, slides the whole camera sideways to the left on wheels or track. The lens stays aimed with the subject while background planes peel past in parallax.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The shot surveys a space or stays with a walker without yawing the head. New information enters from the left as the right side of the room exits.
Because the camera translates, pillars and furniture change their overlap instead of merely sweeping. It is the wrong tool when you only need to look left from a locked tripod.
A pan would rotate; this move relocates.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lay track parallel to the action, horizon locked, height constant. Do not pan to invent the move: the body slides, the lens holds its relative aim.
Subject may stay framed while the world peels, or the camera may discover a new person as it trucks. Prompt a lateral dolly left on track, background planes peeling, subject tracked in frame.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to survey a space or stay with a walker without turning the camera. Concrete beat: sliding along a diner counter so each stool and face arrives in order.
Do not pan from sticks and label it a truck.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Pan Left rotates on a fixed vertical axis with no body travel. A Dolly Right is the same translation the other way: pick the direction that reveals new information.
Tracking Shot often trucks like this while matching a mover's pace; dolly left can also survey a still line of objects.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: There Will Be Blood uses lateral travel to read rooms and landscapes as systems. In the Mood for Love slides along corridors and walls so delay and gossip live in the peeling planes.
Use the side-slip, not the color grade.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Pan Left. The tell is a rotating horizon of objects with no change of station point, and no peeling of near columns against far walls.
The fix is a true sideways translation, level horizon, fixed height.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Dolly Left in film?
It is a lateral truck of the camera body to the left on wheels or track, keeping the lens aimed while space peels in parallax.
Dolly Left vs Pan Left
Pan left turns the head on a locked tripod. Dolly left moves the support sideways, so foreground and background slide at different speeds.
When should I use Dolly Left?
When the next fact is to the left in real space and you want to arrive there by traveling, not by looking. Do not use it if a simple pan connects the two facts.
How do I prompt Dolly Left for AI image or video?
Specify lateral dolly left on track, no pan, locked horizon, visible parallax, subject held in frame. Name what new architecture enters from the left.
